description: Comprehensive health and monitoring dashboard for Ansible Automation Platform. Covers component readiness, service accessibility, job status, latency, and resource usage.

panels.description: The platform gateway is the single entry point for all AAP traffic (UI, API, SSO). If this is down, the entire platform is unreachable.

panels.description: Checks if the AAP web UI is reachable via the platform gateway. The gateway is the single entry point for all AAP traffic. If DOWN, users cannot access any AAP interface.
panels.title: UI Accessible

panels.description: Checks if the AAP controller metrics endpoint (/api/controller/v2/metrics/) is responding to Prometheus scrapes via the gateway. Based on the 'up' metric from the ServiceMonitor. Will also show DOWN during PostgreSQL outages since the metrics endpoint depends on database connectivity.
panels.title: API Accessible

panels.description: Checks if PostgreSQL is reachable via a direct Grafana probe (SELECT 1 against the AAP-PostgreSQL datasource). Independent of Controller metrics scrape and Gateway, so it continues to report true database reachability when the API or UI is down. Works with both cluster-internal and external (RDS, VM) PostgreSQL. If DOWN, Grafana cannot connect to the database (network, authentication, TLS, or database failure) — Controller and Jobs cannot function without it. For external DB, configure the datasource URL/TLS the same way as the Jobs dashboard.
panels.title: PostgreSQL Accessible

panels.description: Controller-observed PostgreSQL application health based on reported database connections and transaction latency. Shows UP when connections are active and latency is normal, DEGRADED when connections are active but commit latency exceeds 1s or event-insert latency exceeds 2s, and DOWN when no connections are reported. Depends on the Controller metrics scrape via the ServiceMonitor, so it may show DOWN when the API is unreachable even if PostgreSQL Accessible (direct probe) remains UP. Does not probe the database directly — use PostgreSQL Accessible for reachability, and this panel to detect database pressure experienced by Controller.

targets.expr: (clamp_max(sum(awx_database_connections_total{namespace=~"$namespace"}), 1) * (1 + clamp_max(((avg(task_manager_commit_seconds{namespace=~"$namespace"}) > bool 1) or (avg(callback_receiver_event_processing_avg_seconds{namespace=~"$namespace"}) > bool 2)), 1))) or on() vector(0)

panels.title: PostgreSQL Health

panels.description: Number of ready Redis cluster replicas. Redis is used for caching, job event queuing, and inter-process communication. A healthy cluster has 6 replicas (3 masters + 3 replicas).
panels.title: Redis Cluster Replicas

panels.description: Redis cluster pod-level health based on StatefulSet replica readiness. Shows HEALTHY when all desired replicas are ready, UNHEALTHY when some or all replicas are down. Does not detect cluster-level issues (e.g., cluster_state:fail, unassigned hash slots) where pods are running but Redis is non-functional. For functional Redis health monitoring, a dedicated Redis probe is recommended.
panels.title: Redis Cluster Health

panels.description: Number of automation jobs currently executing across all controller instances.
panels.title: Running Jobs

panels.description: Jobs waiting in the queue to be picked up by a controller task worker. High pending count may indicate capacity issues.
panels.title: Pending Jobs

panels.description: Total number of jobs that ended in 'failed' or 'error' status. A rising count may indicate playbook issues or infrastructure problems.
panels.title: Failed Jobs

panels.description: Jobs blocked by dependency constraints (e.g., waiting for a parent workflow node to complete). High blocked count may indicate workflow design issues or a failed upstream job holding the pipeline.
panels.title: Blocked Tasks

panels.description: Percentage of total controller capacity (fork slots) currently consumed by running jobs. Yellow at 70%, red at 90% -- indicates the controller is running out of execution capacity.
panels.title: Consumed Capacity

panels.description: Time-series breakdown of all job statuses over time: Running, Successful, Failed, Error, Canceled, Waiting, Pending, and Blocked.
panels.title: Job Launched Statistics

panels.description: Processing time for the controller task manager and callback receiver. High values indicate the controller is slow to process events or start tasks.
panels.title: Controller Processing Time

panels.description: Time spent on PostgreSQL transactions: committing task state, loading pending/workflow tasks from DB, and writing callback events. High values indicate database pressure.
panels.title: PostgreSQL Transaction Latency

panels.description: Time spent in the task manager processing pipeline: loading, starting, and processing running and pending tasks. High values indicate job scheduling bottlenecks.
panels.title: Task Manager Execution Time

panels.description: Total active PostgreSQL connections reported by the Controller metrics endpoint. Red at 0 (no connections), yellow at 1-2 (thin pool), green at 3 or more. A thin or empty pool can indicate Controller-to-database pressure even when PostgreSQL Accessible is still UP. Depends on the Controller metrics scrape, so values may be unavailable when the API is down.
panels.title: DB Connections

panels.description: Highest CPU usage as a percentage of its configured limit across all containers. Green < 70%, Yellow 70-90%, Red > 90%. If red, a container is close to being CPU-throttled.
panels.title: Peak CPU % of Limit

panels.description: Highest memory usage as a percentage of its configured limit across all containers. Green < 70%, Yellow 70-90%, Red > 90%. If red, a container risks being OOMKilled.
panels.title: Peak Memory % of Limit

panels.description: Total CPU cores consumed by all containers in the AAP namespace.
panels.title: Total CPU Cores Used

panels.description: Total working set memory consumed by all containers in the AAP namespace.
panels.title: Total Memory Used

panels.description: Top 5 pods by CPU usage as percentage of their configured limit. Shows instant values. Helps identify which workload is closest to being CPU-throttled.
panels.title: Top 5 CPU Consumers (% of Limit)

panels.description: Top 5 pods by memory usage as percentage of their configured limit. Shows instant values. Helps identify which workload is closest to being OOMKilled.
panels.title: Top 5 Memory Consumers (% of Limit)

panels.description: Callback receiver metrics: Redis event queue depth (events waiting to be written to DB), events held in memory, and average processing time per event. A growing queue indicates the system cannot keep up with event volume. Shows 'No data' when no jobs are running and the callback receiver is idle.
panels.title: Event Processing (Callback Receiver)
